newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finland to buy 21 bln markka in spring '97 - Niinist.
newsitem.headline: Finland to buy 21 bln markka in spring '97 - Niinist.

text.p: Finland will be an active buyer of foreign currencies this spring for state debt servicing needs, Finance Minister Sauli Niinisto said on Wednesday.
"Our (foreign currency) buying will be plentiful in the course of this spring," Niinisto told Reuters by telephone.

On Tuesday, he said in a statement that the government's total 1997 debt service costs, which include repayments and interest payments, on its foreign currency-denominated debt will amount to 42 billion markka ($8.5 billion).

Earlier on Wednesday, Niinisto said "clearly more than half" of that amount would be bought in the spring but later, he corrected his remarks and said "roughly half of that amount will be bought during spring and clearly more than half, before autumn." Niinisto did not give any details.
At end-1996, the state's foreign currency denominated debt was 175.0 billion markka, according to state treasury figures.
